note: Two sets in one file, distinguished by `kind`. kind:'fact' = the research/method statements safe to show in ANY state, including after a miss (they say what the error reveals, never how he should feel). kind:'quote' = attributed motivational lines, decoration only. HARD RULE: a kind:'quote' entry must never be served as a response to struggling, procrastinating or a broken streak — pedagogy-spec §3.5 Playbook P forbids answering those with a motivational quote. Attributions reading 'Attributed to' are traditional, not sourced.

quotes.text: Testing yourself beats rereading. Practice testing lands at d = 0.74 in the meta-analysis; rereading sits near zero.
75 marks in 180 minutes is 2.4 minutes per mark. A 5-mark answer gets 12 minutes, not 25.
The paper has 22 answer-slots: 11 x 1 mark, 8 x 5 marks, 3 x 8 marks. That is a small enough target to drill to saturation.
Skip all three long answers and the ceiling is 51/75 - a B+ at best. Those 24 marks are not optional.
Distributed practice measures d = 0.85 - the largest effect in the table. The same hours, spread out, are worth about a letter grade more than the same hours massed.
Retrieve to criterion, then again days later. Successive relearning measures up to d = 1.82 in real classrooms - roughly ten exam percent.
About 50 to 55 of the 75 marks require applying or extending. Practising recall alone practises the wrong 11 marks.
These methods pay the most to students who are currently behind: d = 0.47, against -0.11 for students already at the top.
Avogadro's number is 6.022 × 10²³ per mole. It counts particles, the way a dozen counts eggs - it is not a mass.
A step-marked answer earns marks line by line. A bare final answer earns one. Formula, substitution, units, significant figures.
Confidently wrong is the most expensive state in the exam hall - and the cheapest to fix once it is visible.
High-load encoding feels worse than rereading while you do it, and tests better afterwards. The discomfort is the technique working.
Concept maps you build yourself: g = 0.72. Concept maps handed to you: g = 0.43. The building is the learning.
Practicals are 25 of every 100 marks, and they are submitted early. Once submitted they are uncorrectable.
A+ needs about 67/75 theory per subject. From 27/75 that is +40 marks - a number you can chase, not a mood.
One correct recall today beats five rereads. Stop the item at criterion; drilling past it buys nothing.
Mole ratios apply to moles, never to grams. Writing the unit on every line is what catches it.
Gravitation and DC circuits carry 10 teaching hours each - the two heaviest units in Grade 11 physics.
Chemistry of non-metals is 22 teaching hours: the single biggest unit in the whole syllabus, and a Group C regular.
Mix problem types within one subject so the method has to be chosen, not remembered. Choosing is the skill the paper actually tests.
Useful feedback says what the error reveals. "Wrong" says nothing; "you used mass where the ratio needs moles" says everything.
Below 70% attendance you cannot sit the exam, whatever your marks look like.
Missing one day does not affect habit formation - the research is clear. Restarting today does.
Implementation intentions - "when X happens, I will do Y" - move follow-through by about d = 0.65. Write the plan, not the wish.
Units and significant figures are marked separately from the answer. They are the cheapest marks in the paper and the most often dropped.
Ray diagrams, circuit diagrams and flowcharts are marked line by line. Memorisers skip them, which is why they are cheap marks.
With OR-choices in about two shorts and one long, reliable mastery of ~85% of the syllabus gives a full choice-set. Less does not.
The floor is 90 seconds and five cards. A night that small still counts, and it is what keeps the interval schedule honest.
Genius is one percent inspiration and ninety-nine percent perspiration.
